topics.topic: India Emerges as Cradle of Jamun Evolution
topics.why_in_news: New palaeobotanical research established India as the evolutionary cradle of Jamun (Syzygium genus) based on fossil discoveries from Early Miocene deposits in Himachal Pradesh.
prelims_quick_notes: Study linked Jamun evolution with East Gondwanan origin.
Fossil evidence discovered from Kasauli Formation in Himachal Pradesh.
New fossil species identified as Syzygium paleosalicifolium.
Study challenges earlier Australian and Southeast Asian origin theories.
Fossil evidence helps reconstruct climatic and evolutionary history.
Study connects Himalayan uplift with vegetation evolution.
Jamun acts as palaeo-climate indicator for monsoon reconstruction.
key_findings_and_indicators: Syzygium traced to East Gondwanan origin around 80 MYA.
11 fossil leaves discovered from Early Miocene deposits.
Evidence suggests India to Southeast Asia to Australia dispersal route.
Continuous presence in India traced since Early Eocene.
Study used 22 morphological characters and statistical validation.
important_facts: Study conducted by Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences (BSIP).
BSIP functions under Department of Science and Technology.
Kasauli Formation associated with Early Miocene fossils.
Palaeobotany studies ancient plant life using fossil evidence.
Biogeography studies spatial and temporal distribution of species.
India was part of East Gondwana before continental drift.
exam_relevance: Important for Geography, Biogeography and Palaeoscience.
Useful for Continental Drift Theory, Gondwana and monsoon evolution topics.
Can be linked with biodiversity, fossil evidence and climate reconstruction.
prelims_traps: Jamun linked with East Gondwanan origin, not recent Southeast Asian origin.
Kasauli Formation located in Himachal Pradesh.
BSIP functions under DST, not Geological Survey of India.
